mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates a contraction in industrial production, which reduces corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST of more than 1% indicates a broad-based weakening in housing and overall demand, which reduces consumer spending and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in FEDFUNDS below 1% combined with a concurrent increase in CPIAUCSL above 4% for two months signals a monetary policy-lag environment where inflation is rising despite easing, which erodes real equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL > 4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 2% for three consecutive months signals a surge in household savings, which typically precedes a reduction in consumption and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
